text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- Special police free three hostages that were held for ten hours by inmates of a high-security prison in southern Graz. The victims, who had been working in the jail's canteen, were unhurt.
- Federal President Thomas Klestil resumes full official duties after recovering from an acute bout of pneumonia that had confined him to hospital for seven weeks.
- About one third of seasonal workers in Austria's tourism industry registered as unemployed by the end of October, up 4.1 percent from a year ago.
- New study shows rising number of Austrians are afraid they may lose their jobs.

- Die Erste savings bank is the largest single participant in a consortium of bidders for privatisation candidate Creditanstalt, expected to make an offer for the bank on Friday. A number of regional banks has left the group.
- Looming end of six-year long Creditanstalt privatisation project drives up the bank's share price.
- Eastern Europe's reform economies have a long way to go to reach western levels of prosperity, Vienna-based Institute for Comparative Studies says.
- Commercial banks overestimate the costs of introducing Europe's planned single currency, central bank board member Dietmar Spranz says.
DIE PRESSE
- President Klestil says his illness was more serious than originally thought.
- Snowstorms hit western Austria, traffic chaos after several main routes across the Alps were closed temporarily.
- Austria's military has initiated disciplinary action against 20 soldiers, part of IFOR peacekeeping troops in Bosnia, for wearing racist T-shirts.
- Belgium's Bacob bank becomes latest addition to the EA-Generali-led consortium of bidders for Creditanstalt.
- Gasoline prices to drop by 0.1 schillings per litre, after increasing as much as 0.3 schillings over the past few weeks amid rising oil price.
KURIER
- Australian-listed Casinos Austria International seeking for partners to help finance its expansion plans overseas.
- Oil and chemicals group OMV remains Austria's largest industrial conglomerate, new compilation of the country's top-500 companies shows.
- Postal union protests against job cuts ahead of planned privatisation of Austria's post and telecoms monopoly.
- Austria's economy is recovering at a slower-than-expected pace, research institute WIFO says.
- Ski-maker Kaestle says it expects a substantial rise in turnover this year.
